newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran spends over $1 billion on petrochemical plant.
newsitem.headline: Iran spends over $1 billion on petrochemical plant.

text.p: Iran has spent over $1 billion on its Tabriz petrochemical plant, the official Iranian news agency IRNA quoted an official as saying on Sunday.

It quoted Mansur Moazami, member of the board of directors of the Petrochemical Industry Company, as saying more than $1 billion has been pumped into the plant due to come on stream by the end of the year.
"With commissioning of the petrochemical plant in Tabriz, polystyrene clear plastic will be produced in Iran for the first time," he said.
Iran is due to bring on stream three petrochemical projects this year, including Tabriz.

The Islamic republic is the second largest petrochemical producer after Saudi Arabia and is aiming to operate six projects at a cost of $3.3 billion in the country's second five-year plan which runs from 1995 to the year 2000.
This is expected to boost Iran's petrochemical capacity to 15 million tonnes a year from the current 10 million tonnes.
